result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md in full, then read domain/qr.ts, the new getMyRegistrations in domain/registration.ts, and handlers/my.ts line by line against the design, plus the export-only diff to handlers/registration.ts and index.ts's registration line. S3 privacy discipline (AC1, the highest-stakes property here) traced structurally, not just read: getMyRegistrations(db, userId) (domain/registration.ts) has exactly one parameter -- userId -- with no eventId/registrationId/tgId or any other caller-suppliable identifier anywhere in its signature, and its single SELECT's only WHERE clause is `eq(registrations.userId, userId)`. handlers/my.ts's only path to a user identity is `resolveActingUser(db, BigInt(tgId))` where tgId comes from `ctx.from.id` (Telegram's own authenticated sender id) -- grepped the whole file for any read from message text/command args/callback_data feeding this path: none exists. Every row's rendering (composeRowText, the QR gate, the withdraw-button eligibility check) uses only fields already present on that same row object (row.eventTitle, row.admission, row.qrToken, etc.) -- no second per-row lookup by any id exists anywhere downstream, confirmed by reading the full handler body (122 lines) with no other `db.` call inside the per-row loop except getWaitlistPosition(db, row.eventId, row.registrationId), which is itself called with THIS row's own ids, never another's. The privacy scoping is genuinely structural, not conventional: there is no argument or code path through which a second user's id could enter this query even by mistake. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC1 MYSELF, not trusted from the report: wrote a throwaway test file apps/bot/src/handlers/my.reviewer-check.test.ts (own fixtures, different shape from BACKEND-DEV's Alice/Bob case -- three users, mixed admission states, a 'secretperson' with a full seeded Profile including company/phone/email plus a raw qrToken, and a 'viewerperson' registered waitlisted for the SAME event) against the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432). Dispatched /my as the viewer via real bot.handleUpdate(), JSON-serialized every captured payload (photo/caption/text/reply_markup, with the InputFile-bearing 'photo' key stripped since its own toJSON() throws), and grepped for the secret user's firstName/lastName/company/phone/email/internal id/qrToken: ZERO occurrences in any of it. The viewer's own registrationId was present exactly where expected (the withdraw button's callback_data). PASS. Deleted the scratch file immediately after; `git status --short` confirmed clean. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC3 MYSELF, not trusted from the report: same throwaway file, a fresh registration with a new qrToken ('q'.repeat(64)), dispatched /my via bot.handleUpdate(), pulled the real InputFile.fileData Buffer off the captured sendPhoto payload, decoded it myself with pngjs (PNG.sync.read) + jsqr (a real QR decoder) -- NOT jsqr against BACKEND-DEV's own fixture, a fresh PNG generated by my own run. Decoded string was byte-for-byte `https://t.me/rev_bot?start=ci_qqqq...q` (64 q's) -- exactly the design's template, using MY test bot's own username ('rev_bot', not 'test_bot'), confirming the botUsername parameter genuinely flows through rather than being hardcoded anywhere. PASS. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC2 MYSELF: own fixture, capacity-0 event, two waitlisted registrations (ahead/viewer) with distinct created_at. Read the viewer's own registrations row's updated_at before invoking /my, invoked /my (which internally calls getWaitlistPosition -- a pure SELECT count, per REQ-021's existing contract, reused unchanged here), then re-read the same row: `updatedAt` was byte-identical (`toEqual`) across the read-before and read-after -- confirms getMyRegistrations/getWaitlistPosition perform zero writes to the viewer's own row, satisfying AC2's 'no write to the viewer's own row' clause independent of BACKEND-DEV's own withdraw-in-the-middle scenario. PASS. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC4 MYSELF: own fixture, one user with four registrations across four distinct events (admitted+qrToken, withdrawn, rejected, waitlisted-at-capacity-0). Dispatched /my, counted captured sendPhoto vs sendMessage calls among the four row-sends (excluding the header preamble): exactly 1 sendPhoto, exactly 3 sendMessage. PASS -- matches the design's admission==='admitted' && qrToken!==null gate exactly. qrcode exact-pin check: apps/bot/package.json's `"qrcode": "1.5.4"` -- read the literal string, no `^`/`~`/range operator present. Same for the four dev dependencies added for real-decode testing (@types/qrcode 1.5.6, jsqr 1.4.0, pngjs 7.0.0, @types/pngjs 6.0.5) -- all five exact-pinned, matching this project's existing dependency-pinning convention (grammy/drizzle-orm/pg in the same file are pinned the same way). Domain logic outside handler bodies (decisions/0004): read handlers/my.ts in full (122 lines). Every decision is delegated: getMyRegistrations (the query), getWaitlistPosition (REQ-021, reused unchanged), decideWithdrawOutcome (REQ-022, reused unchanged, called with actingUser.id as both ownerUserId and actingUserId per the design's own §0.2 reasoning -- 'not-owner' structurally cannot fire from this call site), renderCheckInQrPng (this requirement's own new pure encoder, framework-free, no grammy import, no DbClient dependency -- confirmed by reading domain/qr.ts's full 5-line import list and body). The handler's own logic is composition only: resolving lang, formatting two date/time strings via the existing formatDateTimeInTimezone, string-joining a row's display lines, and branching sendPhoto-vs-sendMessage based on the QR gate's boolean result (not re-deriving that boolean itself -- it directly tests `row.admission === 'admitted' && row.qrToken !== null`, the same predicate the design names, not a business rule invented in the handler). No admission-state, eligibility, capacity, or waitlist-position rule is computed inside handlers/my.ts. Compliant. AC5 (shared QR renderer, not duplicated inline): confirmed handlers/my.ts's only QR-related import is `renderCheckInQrPng` from `../domain/qr.js`, called exactly once (line 110); grepped the file for `qrcode`/`QRCode` -- no match. domain/qr.ts is its own module (not inside registration.ts), exporting one function with no db/ctx dependency, matching the design's own placement reasoning (it performs no I/O, unlike every other export in registration.ts). Compliant -- this is the single shared function REQ-026 is designed to call as a second caller. Withdraw-button reuse (design §0.2): confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts` is EMPTY -- withdraw.ts is genuinely untouched. handlers/my.ts constructs its InlineKeyboard button with callback_data literally `withdraw:confirm:${row.registrationId}` (line 103), the exact string shape WITHDRAW_CONFIRM_PATTERN (defined in withdraw.ts, unchanged) already matches, and index.ts still registers the same, unmodified `makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler(db)` against that pattern -- no new callback pattern, no new handler registration for withdrawal. Compliant. Schema/migration review (decisions/0005, S13): confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/migrations apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` is empty -- no migration in this diff, matching the design's own header claim (registrations.admission/qr_token/event_id/user_id/checked_in_at, events.title/starts_at/ends_at/chapter_id, chapters.timezone all pre-date this run). Not applicable -- no SECURITY-REVIEWER migration sign-off needed for a migration; S3 (privacy) remains the mandatory review surface for Step 2c regardless. Workspace/build-output check: no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (only existing files under apps/bot/src, i18n, docs, handoffs, plus package.json/package-lock.json for the new qrcode/jsqr/pngjs deps, changed). No scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running from BACKEND-DEV's session, reused as-is): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, unchanged, not touched by this diff). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (apps/web Next.js build succeeded; apps/bot's tsc -p tsconfig.json clean). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me. Scope check: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` touches exactly apps/bot/package.json, apps/bot/src/{domain/qr.ts+test, domain/registration.ts, handlers/my.ts+test, handlers/registration.ts (one export keyword), i18n/{en,ru,types}.ts, index.ts (one registration line)}, docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md, this run's own handoffs, and package-lock.json (the five new bot deps) -- exactly the design's own file list, no more, no less.
